---
title: "Hands-on Exercise 1"
subtitle: "Geospatial Data Science with R"
---

This exercise introduces a reproducible geospatial workflow using `sf` and the tidyverse: importing spatial and aspatial data, checking geometry and attributes, managing coordinate reference systems, and performing geoprocessing.

::: {.chapter-link}
[Open the course reference for Chapter 1](https://r4gdsa.netlify.app/chap01.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}
:::

## Learning focus

- Import polygon, line, and point data with `st_read()`.
- Inspect simple-feature objects and their attributes.
- assign or transform coordinate reference systems appropriately.
- Convert longitude/latitude records into an `sf` object.
- Use buffering, spatial intersection, and tidy data wrangling.

## Analysis workflow

1. Acquire and organise the required geospatial and aspatial datasets.
2. Import the datasets using paths that match this project.
3. Inspect their geometry types, attributes, extents, and coordinate systems.
4. Standardise projected data to SVY21 / Singapore TM (EPSG:3414) when distance or area is analysed.
5. Complete and interpret the required geoprocessing tasks.

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
The course website's `chap01/data/...` paths belong to the lecturer's project. Code in this repository must use the actual local data folders instead.
:::
